transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thanks for seeing me. Um, yeah, so I'm here because I just... I can't seem to stay on track with literally anything. The main thing is that I get pulled away by every single little sound or thought that happens around me. It's honestly exhausting. 

Like, just as an example, I’ve been trying to work on this job application, right? Because I really need to get something lined up, so I'll sit down at my laptop and tell myself I'm just going to focus and finish it. But then... a car will drive by outside. Just a normal car, nothing crazy. But my brain latches onto the sound, and suddenly I'm looking out the window wondering where they're going. Or my phone screen will light up out of the corner of my eye, not even a text, just some random notification, and I have to look at it. 

Or even if the room is completely quiet, my own brain is the problem. Some totally random idea will just pop into my head out of nowhere—like I'll suddenly wonder about a movie I watched five years ago, or how something is made—and before I even notice what's happening, I'm completely somewhere else. I'll be twenty tabs deep into the internet or wandering around the room, and the application is just sitting there empty. It’s like every little thing sends me in a completely different direction before I even realize I've stopped doing what I was supposed to be doing in the first place.
Have you experienced this level of difficulty with focus and distractibility since you were a child, or is this a more recent development in your life?

Oh, no, it's definitely not recent. Not at all. It's been like this... well, pretty much my whole life, honestly. I remember way back, like, even in elementary school, it was a whole big thing. My mom used to get so frustrated with me, and the teachers... man, the teachers really did not know what to do with me. 

I mean, they were constantly moving my seat. Like, every other week I was sitting somewhere new—front of the room, back of the room, right next to the teacher's desk—mostly because I just couldn't keep my mouth shut. I'd always be talking out of turn, just blurting things out in the middle of a lesson because whatever popped into my head felt so incredibly urgent right in that exact second, you know? And I'd distract the other kids, so they'd move me again. 

And the schoolwork itself was a total disaster. I was always forgetting my homework. If I actually managed to remember to bring the assignment home, which was a miracle in itself, I'd either forget to do it, or I'd do it and then just leave it sitting on the kitchen counter the next morning. And when we had to do those little worksheets in class? I would just fly through them. I just wanted to be done so I could go do something else, literally anything else, so I'd rush through the whole page as fast as humanly possible. I wasn't even really reading half the questions, so I'd get them back covered in red ink because of all these stupid, careless mistakes. Like, I knew the answers, but I just couldn't slow my brain down enough to actually write them out properly. So, yeah, it’s... it's always been exactly like this. I just never really grew out of it, I guess.
